requirements.statement: The return-code service selects its action from the request type (RC-REQUEST-TYPE): 'I' initialises the return-code area (program ID spaces, current and highest code 0, status SUCCESS, response code 0); 'S' records a new return code; 'G' returns the current code, the highest code and the status with response code 0; 'L' inserts one row into DB2 table RTNCODES with the current timestamp, program ID, current code, highest code, status and message, setting response code 0 when the insert succeeds (SQLCODE 0) and 8 otherwise; 'A' analyses logged codes over a time window. Any other request type performs nothing and leaves the response code unchanged.

When a new return code is set ('S'), if it is greater than the highest code recorded so far (RC-HIGHEST-CODE) it becomes the new highest code; otherwise the highest code is kept. In both cases the current code becomes the new code. The highest code is held in the caller's request area, so it persists only as long as the caller keeps that area.
